blocks.text: Lucy Letby - Examination-in-chief day 2: Babies A, B, C, D, E & F
CONTENTS
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Examination-in-chief by MR MYERS (continued)
Friday, 5 May 2023
(In the absence of the jury)

Before the jury is brought into court, Mr Myers, Mr Johnson, I hope you've seen -- I'm sorry it's been sent to you late -- the email request from the BBC in relation to the release of copies of some of the exhibits.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I haven't had time -- I have seen them but I --
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Can we come back to it then later?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Of course.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Mr Myers?
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: I've only just seen it, my Lord.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: All right, we'll come back -- if you could perhaps -- this afternoon we'll come back to it. It won't take very long. It's obviously something of which you're aware because there's been discussion and the CPS actually suggested the BBC contact me. That's what it says here.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: All right. I've got the gist and I have forwarded it to the person that it needs to go to, so that person I can discuss it.
blocks.speaker: MR JOHNSON

blocks.text: Absolutely, yes. It's not urgent.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR JUSTICE GOSS

blocks.text: (In the presence of the jury)
MS LUCY LETBY (continued)
Examination-in-chief by MR MYERS (continued)
Ms Letby, we're going to go to count 1 on the indictment, which is the case of [Baby A]. What I'll do, as we
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: go through these counts on the indictment, is just to remind us all, for your benefit and for the benefit of the ladies and gentlemen on the jury, briefly of the details relating to the birth of the baby we're looking at and then, either at the outset or when we come to it at an appropriate place, we'll look at any relevant nursing notes, particularly the ones that are written by you. All right? That's how we'll deal with it. We'll be assisted with that.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: There will be an amount of moving between the documents, ladies and gentlemen, like the interviews and the charts, so if you can keep an eye on where your files are and we will take our time to make sure we've got the right material, and you too, Ms Letby.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: [Baby A]. I'm going to ask if we can put up tile 1, please. Thank you, Mr Murphy. If we go inside that, please.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: We can see the name [Surname of Babies A & B], referred to on the indictment as [Baby A], mother [Mother of Babies A & B].
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: [Baby A] was born on 7 June 2015. We see elsewhere in fact, but we see that's at 20.31, so just after 8.30 in the evening, on 7 June at 31 weeks and 2 days. He was the second of the twins, twin 1 was his sister, [Baby B], and we can see here his weight is 1,660 grams. So born by caesarean.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Could we go to tile 3, please. We'll go into that.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: This sets out those details. Can we go behind that, please? Scroll down if you would, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: [Baby A] was born with antiphospholipid syndrome.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: There's the maternal history of high blood pressure and a previous stroke, so medication for that.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: The event that we're looking at in count 1 is on the evening of 8 June and we will come to the details shortly. But just to remind us, 8 June. And at 20.05, there was a 10% dextrose infusion that began with [Baby A] via the long line. At 20.26, he collapsed and sadly died at 20.58 that evening.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: We'll just look at the notes that deal with that and then we'll move to the questions, Ms Letby. But this is to assist you and everybody. The first note I'm going to go to, with your assistance, Mr Murphy, is the note by Melanie Taylor at tile 224. Could we go into that, please? Can we enlarge the text section on the right-hand side? If you could enlarge first of all the entry on the centre of the right-hand side. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I'm going to pick this up from the entry at 19.05, so this is before the shift when you came on, Ms Letby.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: 8 June, 19.05, by Melanie Taylor. It says:
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: "UVC in wrong position. Reinserted SHO MacCarrick. Again in wrong position. Cannula tissued. Doctors busy on ward 30. Aware no fluids running for a couple of hours. Long line inserted by Registrar Harkness. Awaiting X-ray. Remains settled on N CPAP. Enteral feeds of donor EBM started at 1ml two-hourly."
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: That's the note at 19.05. I'm going to go next to the note at 21.28 that follows that and goes over the page. At 21.28, which is after the event, Nurse Taylor put this in:
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: "Observations stable. Pink, well perfused. UVC still in situ but in wrong position. To be used if no other access available."
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Then over the page, if we read on, please:
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: "Long line inserted by registrar Dr Harkness. Secured, X-rayed. 10% dextrose run through and connected to long line. 10% dextrose run as per Dr Harkness until line confirmed. Care handed over to Lucy Letby at 20.00. Before leaving, apnoea/heart rate dropped. Cardiac compressions and resus commenced. See documentation by Lucy Letby and medical notes."
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: So we'll turn to that and then we will ask you some questions, Ms Letby. Could we go to tile 228, please, Mr Murphy? These are your notes, Ms Letby, in effect following on.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: So we go into that and it starts at the bottom right:
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: "Written in retrospect."
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: This a note at 07.56, I should say, on 9 June, so the following morning:
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: "Care taken over at 20.00. Emergency equipment checked. Fluids calculated. [Baby A] nursed on CPAP."
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Details there. If we go over the page, though, please:
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: "Observations: stable at 20.05. 10% glucose commenced via long line with Staff Nurse Taylor as agreed by Reg Harkness who was present. UVC remained in situ from day shift. Instructed line not to be used by reg. [Baby A] noted to be jittery. Was due to have blood gas and blood sugar taken. At 20.20 [Baby A]'s hands and feet noted to be white, centrally pale and poor perfusion. [Baby A] became apnoeic, Registrar Harkness in the nursery and assistance called for. 10% glucose infusion disconnected
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: immediately. [Baby A] making nil respiratory effort. Neopuffed with Guedel airway. Shortly after no heart rate detected and full resuscitation commenced as per medical notes. UVC used to administer drugs. Parents and maternal grandmother present. Dr Jayaram in attendance throughout. [Baby A] passed away at 20.58 and was given to parents to cuddle."
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I'm going to stop at that point, Ms Letby.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: If we need any more detail it's there. That's just to assist us with what we're dealing with with count 1, so I'm going to ask to take that down from the screen for the time being, Mr Murphy. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I want to pause before we turn to the events that night and just remind ourselves, just to get some context, we're looking at the middle of 2015, June 2015.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: Do you recall where you were living round about this time, Ms Letby?
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS

blocks.text: I moved around that time.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I wonder if you could put up, to remind us, exhibit J355, please, Mr Murphy. We saw this when we last looked at your evidence. We know the events with [Baby A] are the 8th into 9 June:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "1 June, Ash House."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So what do we know happened on 1 June?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's where I moved to.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Hen party in York on 5 June?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Had you settled back into Ash House by the time we're dealing with the events with [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No. I was still in the process of moving and unpacking.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Do you recall whether you'd been expecting to come in on that evening shift of 8 June?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, I was -- I received a text message from Yvonne Griffiths, the deputy manager, asking me to work that morning.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Could we have a look, please, at tile 69, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We're going to look at a series of messages starting at tile 69. This is from Yvonne Griffiths to you, 8 June, 9.21 in the morning. So a little under 12 hours before the event we're looking at:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Morning, Lucy, hope you had a lovely weekend. Just wondering if you can split your nights this week and work tonight and tomorrow and come off Thursday and Friday."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: If we go to the following tile, tile 70, you reply at 9.22:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Yes, that's fine. Is it busy?"
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So would you have known you were due to be called in to assist before these messages?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You've asked if it's busy. Can we go to tile 71, response by Yvonne Griffiths:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Oh thank you, Lucy. We have three on CPAP, singleton Sat and twins last night, all 30-weekers, so just wanted six staff on, thanks."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Tile 72, please. You now to Jennifer Jones-Key:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Sorry I was in bed. Hope you slept. I'm working tonight and tomorrow now as busy."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Just pausing there, was it unusual to get requests to come in like this over this period?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, it happened frequently.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Were you often requested to do that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And did you assist?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: As much as I was able to, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Why were you ready to do that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I was very flexible. As I say, I lived locally, I had no commitments outside of work, so I was very happy to help when I could and adapt my shifts as needed.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You went in for the evening shift; is that right?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And we can see, and let's remind ourselves, the layout for that. That's on tiles 161 and 162. So can we go to 161, please.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Monday, 8 June at 19.30. Could you just help us, when it's the evening shift, do you regard it as the 19.30 shift or a 20.00 shift? What time do you regard it as starting?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I'm not going to read out everything that we can see there but we can see who you're on with. If we go to tile 162 to see who is designated with which baby. You were the designated nurse for [Baby A], weren't you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: At this stage of the sequence of events, we don't have the nurseries marked on. That came with the diagrams later, but we know [Baby A] and [Baby B] were both in nursery 1; is that right?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's right.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You remember that, do you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: When did you first learn that you'd be caring for [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: When I arrived on unit that evening and was told at handover that's who I would be allocated to.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And do you recall what time you would have got to the unit?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I would have been ready to start my shift at 19.30.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember what followed? We've got the notes but do you have any recollection independent of the notes of what followed?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, I do, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We'll go back over things in the detail we need to but could you start by telling us what happened? You get there that evening for the shift to start. We know that Mel Taylor had been looking after [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's right.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Can you describe events from the time that you get on to the unit?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So I received the group handover that we get at the start of a shift and I knew that I'd been allocated to look after [Baby A] in nursery 1. I went straight into nursery 1 to get handover then from Melanie Taylor. At that point there was a lot of activity going on in the nursery.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Pause there for a moment.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You find out then that you're looking after [Baby A]; is that right?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's right.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You go into the nursery. Do you recall who was in the nursery or do you not?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, so Melanie Taylor was in the nursery and Dr Harkness was in there doing a procedure.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: When you refer to there being activity in there, is that what you mean or is there something else that sticks in your mind?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So I remember there was just a lot going on in the nursery, the lights were up full, I think Dr Harkness was doing a line procedure at the time, and I remember Melanie Taylor was preparing fluids for [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. You went into nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What happened once you went into nursery 1?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I went into nursery 1 and Melanie Taylor was there, preparing fluids for [Baby A], and she explained that [Baby A] had been without fluids for a few hours because he'd needed a line inserting, and as a priority we got straight on with connecting those fluids to [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. You say [Baby A] -- she explained he'd been without fluids for some hours?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: She did, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Could we look at tile 35, which is the intensive care chart for this period for [Baby A]. If we go behind that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And if we just start with this, actually, we can see this is for 8 June, Ms Letby, for [Baby A], it says [Baby A]. We're familiar with the charts now so I'm going to ask if we could scroll down. We can see up to 16.00, there are entries, and then at 16.00 that day for [Baby A] it says "cannula tissued".
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And apart from an entry for NGT, at 18.00, which is some expressed breast milk via the NGT, what does that tell us, the fact after 16.00 the various readings have stopped?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So after that point at 16.00 his peripheral line has tissued which means he can no longer receive IV fluids.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So at that point, from 16.00 onwards, or between 16.00 and 20.00, he didn't have any fluids running.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's what was explained to you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That had been stopped?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: There's something else I would like to ask you about.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It is on tile 145. There's reference to a line that had been positioned. It's at tile 145, please. It's in Dr Harkness' clinical notes. As a general rule I'm not going to be taking you through clinical notes, but where there's something in them I would like you to assist us with I will. If we scroll to the bottom of that page we can see something in Dr Harkness' notes that said "X-ray review". It's a sticker, it says the time of the X-ray. For the date it's got 8 June 15, 19.09. And there's a description of what's there, but under "Comments" it says:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Long line at right subclavian/SVC [which is superior vena cava]. To be pulled back."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Can you see that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's what it was saying at 19.09. Were you aware that there was a repositioning of the long line that was due to take place? Had that been explained to you?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I was told at that time that the line was suitable for use.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You were told it was suitable for use?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And who told you that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Melanie Taylor and Dr Harkness.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Is that the line that the 10% glucose went down?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We can take that down, please, Mr Murphy. Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Can you explain then what happens next? You say that Melanie Taylor had been getting ready.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, when I entered the nursery Melanie Taylor was dressed sterilely, which is what we need to do to prepare fluids. She had the IV fluid trolley out and had the fluids and had gloves and apron on and was starting to run through some fluids into the line. And when I arrived in the nursery, we decided a this that would be our priority, we would both check the fluids, get those running on [Baby A] and then have a formal handover.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So we know you get on to the unit round about, not precisely, 7.30.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If it's possible, how far into getting on to the unit would this conversation and these arrangements start with [Baby A]?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: First we would have had collective handover at the nurses' station before that, so that would have taken 20 minutes or so, maybe, even more.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Then you go to the nursery?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's right.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And then when you're in the nursery, that's where you begin to make arrangements with Melanie Taylor?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. Can you tell us who was going to do what with regard to running fluids through the line?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So when you're running fluids through a long line one member of staff has to be sterile and that person was Melanie Taylor.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What does that mean when you say sterile? What have they done or how are they that means they are the sterile nurse?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So that nurse is wearing gloves and an apron. They have sterilised the whole of the area that we're working with. We have a fluids trolley, they would have sterilised the area. And then any of the fluids that they're touching, the connections that go to it, that is all kept sterile.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: We've heard it involves two nurses for this. What's the other nurse doing?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So you have to have a role then of a dirty nurse, which is the person who does the things such as connecting it to the pump and doing any of the practical things that that person can't touch because they're sterile.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So who was going to be doing that when it came too [Baby A] and the dextrose?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I was the one that was the dirty nurse that would be programming the pump.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Was it a premade bag of dextrose that was used?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, it was.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Where would that have come from?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So Mel had it out when I arrived, but the bags are kept in nursery 1 in the cupboard.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It was already out when you got there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, it was. It was all on the trolley ready.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So the bag's ready, Melanie Taylor was the sterile nurse, you were going to assist. What happened next?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So we went to [Baby A]'s cot side. Mel finished connecting the fluids and drawing them through the line.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: She then went to [Baby A] to attach the fluids and I turned my attention then to hanging the bag and programming the pump.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Right. So can you give us a little more detail? Who was doing what with which bit of the equipment?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: At that time Mel is the one who is handling the bag of 10% and the infusion line that runs with that. She was then the one that would physically go to [Baby A], clean the long line and attach that to the line.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: What does that involve, attaching it to the line, just so we can follow? What actually does that mean?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: You have to access the line, you clean the line with an alcohol wipe to make the area sterile. She would then have needed to flush the line to check that it was patent. And after that then you would connect the fluid line to the end of the long line.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: I can imagine there's a line coming down from the bag and the apparatus there.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: When you're talking about connecting it, what is it being connected to so far as [Baby A] is concerned?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It'd be connected to the port that's coming out of the long line that's in [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So the line that had been positioned by Dr Harkness?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember where it was coming out of [Baby A], where the port was?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: His left arm.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So that's what's being connected?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And who's doing that connecting?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Melanie Taylor because she's the one who's sterile.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And then could you repeat, what is it that you were doing whilst she did that?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So I was responsible for hanging the 10% bags, that's putting it onto the drip stand next to the cot side, and then programming the pump.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And is that what happened?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And you mentioned about the line, did you say, being flushed to make sure it's patent?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, the usual practice is whenever you are attaching something to any line you would flush the line with sodium chloride first to check that the line is working.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: That's usual -- that's standard practice?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's standard practice, really, for anything going through a line, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And did that happen?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I can't -- I wasn't watching Mel specifically but that is usual practice, yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: If we please look at tile 174, which is the IV prescription chart. Help us with the time. Go behind that, please, Mr Murphy.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: We can see here:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "8 June, 10% dextrose, 500ml bag."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And it's got a rate there. "Route" -- what does it say under "route"?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Long line."
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It's been prescribed by or which registrar?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Dr Harkness.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And then it says "given by". Who's the -- is it your signature there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, my signature's on the bottom.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: You say Melanie Taylor also gave it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So that's the other signature?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Let me just ask you this because others have been asked it: is there a clear significance to whose name goes where as to above or under when it's a signature?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, not at all, no.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: It says "Date and time started". It looks like -- can you tell us what that says?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I say that's 20.05.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So five past eight in the evening?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And is it you that wrote that in or Mel or someone else?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Do you know?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It would have been myself or Mel. I can't say.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: One or other?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: Do you remember who?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: And what does that tell us?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That is the exact time that the fluids began to run through the pump.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. Is that what took place?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: So 10% dextrose begins to go down the line?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Yes, we would only sign for it once we were happy that the fluid was actually infusing through the line.
blocks.speaker: LETBY

blocks.text: All right. So --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So at this point it has been connected and the pump is running.
blocks.speaker: LETBY
